Best Indian Restaurant in hcm
Aug 2025 • Couples
Recently, I enjoyed a dinner for two at Dalcheeni in Hồ Chí Minh City and it was a delightful experience. For our meal, we ordered biryani, aloo kulcha, and fish tikka masala, with the total cost around 400,000 VND—quite reasonable for the atmosphere and service.

The biryani was aromatic and well-cooked, with each grain of rice carrying a gentle mix of spices and perfectly tender meat. The aloo kulcha was warm and crispy outside, with a tasty potato filling, making it a great side. The fish tikka masala was a real highlight: the fish was juicy and fresh, swimming in a rich, flavorful sauce that was both creamy and nicely spiced, but not overwhelming.

Dalcheeni’s interior is tastefully decorated with classic Indian elements, making the dinner feel cozy and a bit special, ideal for a date. The staff were attentive and quick to serve, always cheerful and happy to help us understand the menu. I really appreciated how clean and inviting the space was, adding to the positive impression.

Overall, Dalcheeni offered excellent Indian dishes and a romantic atmosphere at a fair price. I was satisfied by both the flavors and the experience, and would recommend this place to anyone in Saigon who enjoys quality Indian cuisine and a welcoming dining environment.

Dear Dalcheeni
Apr 2024 • Couples
I don't know how to express my gratitude. We have spent many beautiful nights at this restaurant that will color our lives.
We love India and have visited there many times, but this restaurant offers a more elegant and deep flavor than any other food we have eaten there. 
We are Japanese, and there are very few sophisticated Indian restaurants in Japan. At first, I was not familiar with Indian food.But thanks to this restaurant, I was able to learn the real taste.
I think people who visit here can feel the majestic and rich land of India just by imagining what spices are used and how they are cooked.

The sophisticated interior and beautifully set tables are perfect for scenes where you face your loved ones.

This restaurant has so many menus that it may be difficult for those who are not familiar with India to order. But don't worry. There is a guide here who will guide you through a wonderful night. His name is Jiban. If you get lost, just call out to him and his wife and you will have the best time. They are friendly, kind, and compassionate like Indians. They are our best friends.

The cocktails here are also of a high level, so you should definitely try them. All the dishes offer a perfect taste, so you will not fail no matter what you eat. I will post the photos of my recommended menu.

Meeting the best friends at this restaurant is a treasured event in our lives. Thank you so much. I look forward to seeing you again.

Racist remark - Being an Indian himself, he had the audacity to tell us that we Indians create too much fuss!!! Slow claps for him!!

Dalcheeni - decent Indian food in HCMC
Dec 2023 • Family
This is a good restaurant, conveniently located close by a few hotels. 
My wife and I are huge fans of Indian food, I've visited the country dozens of times for work and we wanted to fulfill our need for Indian food after mostly dining at Vietnamese restaurants during our trip. 
Dalcheeni is a clean, bright and spacious restaurant. 
The menu is extensive; separated into different styles/regions of cuisine, which is a nice touch if not a little tricky to navigate for an inexperienced diner. Staff friendly, would've been good to have been told about the kids menu (didn't spot it until after we ordered).
Good wine selection, spotted a personal favourite. Mango Lassi was fantastic. 
All dishes and drinks arrived well presented.
In terms of the food, mutton curry was very nice. The Dal was a little creamier than we are used to, but was good. Curry full of flavour, paneer really good, possibly a speciality for this restaurant. Tandoori chicken was OK. Not one to speculate; I was a little unwell the following day, my wife to a lesser extent. 
Would say worth a visit if you're looking for Indian cuisine in HCMC

They catered a family Vietnamese/Indian wedding in Nha Trang on July 3rd. The wedding buffet was amazing, for me especially the grilled lamb chops and authentic tandoori roti. It simply was the best vindaloo I have ever tasted, spicy but flavorful where the “heat” added to the flavor versus dominating it. Big chunks of lamb with bone which is true homestyle cooking, with thick sauce and amazing buttery roti kulcha to mop it up. The other lamb dishes were Gosht Nihari and Mutton Rara were similarly exquisitely flavored. The vegetarian dishes ordered by others in our group drew similar comments - the best of flavored authentic indian food. The tea drinkers in our group were impressed with the flavor and spice combination in their chai. Even the humble dhal, brought back memories of well flavored and balanced ingredients from my childhood in Trinidad. I unabashedly recommend their food. Indian restaurants are usually middle of the road in their approach to non-indial palates. Dalcheeni remains true to the best of Indian cuisine, homestyle with depth and balance of flavor while remaining unpretentious and exquisite at the same time - a rare and remarkable achievement!

The rice tasted as though it had had butter added to it which I couldn't warm too at first but fortunately the curry soon took away the buttery flavour. We also shared a dal curry - I forget which one - which was pleasant enough but not really with the wow factor. On further visits I sampled the extremely delicious Murgh Bawli Handi which was a super tasty chicken curry with yellow chilies and onions. My husband had the lamb chops with the ginger, onions and yogurt, which he said was refreshingly different, and a friend enjoyed her Gobi Manchurian, saying that it was one of the best she had tasted anywhere. They both very much also enjoyed the Tandoori Broccoli which they shared as a side. Since then we have been many times to Dalcheeni, a super smart restaurant with very professional staff, and now have found particular favourites. My husband always enjoys a regular feast of very tasty hot and sour soup, followed by Lamb Rogon Josh and my friend and I cannot get enough of the Vegetable Kadi and a fantastic dish called Mirch Baingan Ka Salan. I never remember the name of the dish so I normally ask the waiter for the baby aubergine and chili curry. The last 2 dishes mentioned are quite possible the best curries ever eaten anywhere and are nothing like the vegetable kadai found in other Indian restaurants and I don't think the baby aubergine and chili curry even exists in other restaurants. I don't normally have veggie curries but these 2 are so exceptional that I could eat them daily! They are also the 2 best curries a friend has ever eaten, as well. The fried poppadoms ( called Appalam in Dalcheeni) are very pleasant and their home made mixed pickle is the best ever! It is a restaurant we plan to return to return to again and again as there is always a culinary delight waiting.
